web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained authorized prologue excerpt narrates John Clark and other characters externally as he, she, and they while freely reporting Clark's thoughts; no participating narrator frames the scenes.

web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly describes the entire tale as third-person omniscient and explains that the narration moves among the knowledge and thoughts of Popov, Clark, and other characters.

search_log: Searched for "Tom Clancy Rainbow Six excerpt chapter one" and publisher/author excerpts; opened the Penguin Random House excerpt and the Tom Clancy author-site PDF.
Searched for "Rainbow Six Tom Clancy third person point of view narrator"; opened BookRags' whole-book point-of-view discussion.

Searched Penguin Random House, Hachette, Google Books, and Open Library variants; Hachette supplied catalog material but no opened prose excerpt, Google Books produced no usable result, and unrelated game guides were discarded.

Searched for "Rainbow Six" with first person, multiple narrators, epistolary, and frame narrative; results were dominated by first-person-shooter video-game material and produced no credible evidence of alternating novel narration.

Searched exact clipped quote fragments, including "we're proceeding on the assumption" and "Foster poured some more bourbon"; Goodreads repeated the fragments without restoring attribution, and an unauthorized full-text mirror was not used as evidence.
person_note: The quote evidence and web research agree on a nonparticipating third-person narrator. In particular, q00556 reports Popov's thought externally and q00559 gives a sustained external profile of Loiselle; the authorized opening likewise narrates Clark and several other characters externally while entering their thoughts. The whole-book point-of-view description confirms that this structure controls the entire novel. The isolated we in q00572 lacks boundaries and attribution and therefore cannot establish a first-person section, while q00574's I is plainly dialogue. Several other quotes are too short or expository to diagnose person, but none supplies credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration. The remaining uncertainty is limited to attribution of the clipped fragments, not the book-level person.
